primary_statement.text: Exercise 6.78. Show that simple random walk (\Psi_j,X_j) on the Cayley graph of \Z^{\odot} (with the standard generators) satisfies p_{2n}(o,o) >= exp(-Cn^{1/3}) for some C and all n. (The matching upper bound was proved in Corollary 6.32(iii).)
primary_statement.note: Printed once, in the collected in-text exercises of Chapter 6; no body theorem, proposition, lemma or example of the fixed version cites Exercise 6.78 by number, so there is no second body occurrence of the number. The group symbol is transcribed as \Z^{\odot} from the root session's full-resolution viewing of this page; see the reader's literal-feature item 1 and this draft's pixel_inspection_status.

full_support_proof.route: Take any starting point v in [-r,r]. The Comment asserts, for some constant c, that with probability at least e^{-c} the walk stays within distance 2r of the origin up to time r^2 and is within distance r of it at time r^2; this block-confinement estimate is asserted, not derived, and the reader keeps it as asserted. Applying the Markov property repeatedly at times that are multiples of r^2 then gives a lower bound e^{-c\lceil n/r^{2}\rceil} for staying inside [-2r,2r] up to time 2n. Adding the requirement that each lamp in [-2r,2r] is switched off at the last visit to it, and that the lamplighter returns to the origin, converts this into p_n(o,o) >= exp(-cn/r^{2}-c_{1}r). Optimising suggests r = n^{1/3}, which yields the exp(-Cn^{1/3}) lower bound the exercise asks for; the Comment closes by citing Pittet and Saloff-Coste (1999).
full_support_proof.completeness: The author prints the whole chain from the block estimate to the optimisation sentence. Nothing in the argument is supplied by this reader. The three points the adjudication records as residual are all preserved literally and none is filled in: the exercise writes p_{2n}(o,o) while the Comment writes p_n(o,o) (kept side by side, since the estimate is uniform in n and the substitution is a relabelling); the block-confinement constant c is asserted rather than derived inside the Comment (kept as asserted); and the ceiling \lceil n/r^{2}\rceil is left as printed, with no n/r^2 + 1 absorption and no assembly of C from c and c_1 written in.
